model_card.summary: A trained bigram and context-1/3/5 character MLPs, with their embedded training vocabularies.
model_card.scope: Inspect next-character probability tables and context-length/parameter trade-offs on 12 controlled colour/shape documents.
limitations: The custom split contains only 9/1/2 train/validation/test documents. This is a controlled continuation exercise, not general Chinese language or instruction-following capability.
These checkpoints use a separate character schema: boundary/EOS=0, unseen character/UNK=1. They do not use the 264-ID ByteTokenizer or TinyLM chat markers.

Each simple-v1 file contains model, vocabulary, kind, context and width for inference. The backup directory preserves all artifacts, but these checkpoint files contain no optimizer or RNG state and cannot reproduce an exact resumed training trajectory.
Context length and parameter count both change between variants. A lower held-out NLL on this tiny split does not establish a universal best context size.
NLL is per next-character target including EOS boundaries; it is not directly comparable with the byte/BPE experiments or broad task accuracy.

evaluation.nll_measurement: All after-NLL values are evaluated at the same final post-update time; generation tables and raw documents are omitted.

training_data.source: Twelve program-generated Chinese colour/shape documents, split before training-vocabulary construction
training_data.modifications: Program-generated controlled records; family-level split before training.
training_data.vocabulary: Training-set characters only; each checkpoint embeds its own exact mapping. vocabulary.json is an optional inspectable copy.

review.scope: Reviewed four completed simple-v1 CPU inference checkpoints, embedded character vocabularies and optional vocabulary JSON hashes, 9/1/2 document split and context/parameter comparison limits. These files contain no optimizer/RNG resume state. Remote release still requires native reconstruction and anonymous pinned-file roundtrip.
